pattern_id: Crash-time vote persistence allows double voting and potential dual leaders in same term
description: This pattern captures a class of Raft election-safety bugs where a node can grant more than one vote in the same term after a crash that tears the atomicity of voting-related stable state. In HashiCorp Raft, the RequestVote handler first updates currentTerm durably via setCurrentTerm(term) and only later persists lastVoteTerm/lastVoteCand via persistVote(term,candidate). If a crash occurs between these two writes, the node may restart with currentTerm = T but lastVoteTerm < T and a stale lastVoteCand. On receiving a new RequestVote(term=T) from a different candidate, the node’s check `lastVoteTerm == req.Term && lastVoteCandBytes != nil` fails, so it treats the request as a fresh election and grants another vote in term T. In a suitably orchestrated network partition, this enables two different candidates to each obtain a majority in the same term T, leading to dual leaders and potentially conflicting committed entries. The characteristic test shape is: (1) start a multi-node cluster and reach a stable term with equal logs, (2) partition the current leader to force a new election in term T+1 and ensure victim node V has voted for candidate C1, (3) simulate a crash-time race by manually corrupting V’s stable store to keep currentTerm=T+1 while regressing lastVoteTerm and lastVoteCand, then restart V, (4) isolate C1 and send a RequestVote(term=T+1) from a different candidate C2 to V, and (5) assert that V must not grant a second vote in term T+1 and that, once the cluster is healed, there is at most one leader per term and no index/term pair holds different commands across nodes. A vulnerable implementation will grant the second vote in step (4) and may in more elaborate topologies produce simultaneous leaders in the same term.
trigger_condition: A node processes a RequestVote(term=T) by durably updating currentTerm to T but crashes before persisting lastVoteTerm/lastVoteCand; after restart its state satisfies currentTerm=T but lastVoteTerm<T. A later RequestVote(term=T) from a different candidate arrives while the original candidate is partitioned away, and the RequestVote logic only checks for an exact match on (lastVoteTerm == req.Term && lastVoteCand!=nil) to detect prior voting, allowing a second vote in term T.
test_template: 1) Start a Raft cluster of N>=3 voting nodes using an in-memory or controllable StableStore and transport. 2) Allow the cluster to elect an initial leader and replicate several benign commands so logs and commitIndex are equal. 3) Partition the original leader away from a majority so that a follower in the majority times out and starts an election for term T+1; identify that follower as C1 and select another follower V in the same partition as the victim. 4) Issue an explicit RequestVote(term=T+1, lastLog=*cluster*) RPC from C1 to V and assert that V grants the vote, ensuring its lastVoteTerm/lastVoteCand are set for term T+1. 5) Simulate the crash window between setCurrentTerm and persistVote by directly mutating V’s StableStore: keep keyCurrentTerm at T+1 but set keyLastVoteTerm to some stale value < T+1 and keyLastVoteCand to an arbitrary old candidate; then hard-stop V and restart a new Raft instance over the same stores and snapshot store. 6) After restart, verify that V’s in-memory currentTerm equals T+1 while stable lastVoteTerm<T+1, confirming the crash-torn vote state. 7) Reconnect the cluster, then re-partition so that C1 is isolated and a different candidate C2 (e.g., the original leader or another follower) can communicate with V. Clear V’s notion of any leader if necessary. 8) From C2’s transport, send a new RequestVote(term=T+1, lastLog=V’s last entry) to V and assert that V must NOT grant this vote (resp.Granted==false); this enforces per-term vote uniqueness despite the torn durable vote. 9) Optionally heal the cluster, wait for a stable leader, and scan all nodes’ states to assert that for every term t there is at most one node in Leader state with currentTerm==t and that for all committed indices i and term t no two nodes store different commands at (i,t).
